title: An accented over-long line is cut earlier and never in the middle of a letter
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin (all permissions) at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) on the What/Why QA build.
  • Require Tech Story (Settings, Work Orders tab) is off.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A08 Fleet) has a contact person and an asset, {Asset-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A08 Truck).
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S2-15440) is open for {Customer-A} and {Asset-A} at {Location-A}, not invoiced.
  • {Work-order-1} has a labor line {Line-1} whose Title is exactly 16 characters (for example ZZAUTOTEST-WW-A8) and whose Description is the letter é repeated 3,000 times, with no tech story.
  • {Work-order-1} has been completed and invoiced as invoice {Invoice-A} (for example 10234), dated {Invoice-date-A} (for example 13 Oct 2026).
custom_steps:
1. Open the Reports page and click Export Reports (if it is not there, open it from Administration).
  2. Choose the Customer Invoice report.
  3. Set the date range to cover {Invoice-date-A}.
  4. Download the report.
  5. Open the downloaded file in a spreadsheet (for example Google Sheets: File, Import, Upload).
  6. Find the row for {Line-1} on invoice {Invoice-A} and read its ItemDescription cell.
  7. Click an empty cell, type =LEN( then click that ItemDescription cell, type ) and press Enter.
  8. Click another empty cell, type =RIGHT( then click the ItemDescription cell, type ,5) and press Enter.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 6: the cell holds the title, " - ", then a run of é letters, and is far shorter than the full 3,019 characters. No odd symbol such as � or Ã© appears anywhere.
  • Step 7: the number is 2,009 (16 + 3 + 1,990 letters é). Each é takes two units of the 4,000 limit, so 19 + 1,990 x 2 = 3,999 units fit and one more é would need 4,001. This plain-looking line is cut much earlier than a line of plain digits of the same length.
  • Step 8: the last five characters are "ééééé": the last letter is a whole é, not half of one and not a �.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-11257; story SV-10132 (Story 3, What Reaches QuickBooks); PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It (What/Why)", Confluence 845348896, version of 13 Oct 2026, S3-R7, S3-R7a, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 2.2 (The long end), 13 Oct copy; tech plan "Title and Description - Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 2026-09-23, shared by the QA lead 13 Oct 2026), FR-011; Product comment by Chris Ward, 23 Sep 2026 (Confluence comment 883261444); Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (a What/Why QA build exists; verification by the build verification session).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R7: “When the joined text is longer than 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end to fit, and it is never cut in the middle of a character. The live sync and the downloadable report are both cut at that same limit, so S3-R4 holds on a long line too. Today only the live sync cuts, and it cuts by bytes without regard for where a character ends; the report has no cut at all. Because the title leads and the narrative trails, the title always survives and the narrative is what gets clipped first.”
  • S3-R7a: “The limit is a storage limit rather than a count of what a reader sees, so a line written with accented or non-Latin characters may be shortened more than an English line that looks the same length on screen. Two lines that look equally long can therefore be cut at different points. That is correct behavior and not a defect.”
  • Tech plan FR-011: “If the joined text exceeds 4,000 bytes it is shortened from the end, never mid-character, on both routes; title survives; an over-long line still syncs (S3-R7, S3-R7a, S3-E3).”
